label: copy phase, later recall positions (boosted by input u / 2)
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase feature: 98% of activation mass is at copy steps (t > L), and it is essentially silent during the original tokens and at <DEL>. It never fires at the first-occurrence input of a token. The firing rate ramps up with recall position, from 6% at recall_idx 1 to 45% at recall_idx 8, and with absolute t. It is also strongly token-modulated: an input u (45% rate, 21% of mass) or 2 (31%) fires it most, out_tok u has 5.5x lift, and the strongest activations (up to 0.67) are on u u runs being re-copied, ramping through the 1-2 tokens before u. Within the copy phase the feature is dense, firing on about 25% of steps, so precision is low (~0.34). No simple token or position predicate gets F1 above ~0.58.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: u, 2, i, t; t=10: u, 2, t, i; t=11: u, 2, t, w) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: u, 0, y, g; copy phase: u, 2, i, g; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: to_go=0, recall_idx=4, phase=2.
